questions.prompt: The total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
Atoms are created during a chemical reaction.
questions.explanation: False — no atoms are created or destroyed.

questions.prompt: When a gas escapes, mass is truly lost from the reaction.
questions.explanation: False — the gas still has mass; if trapped, total mass is unchanged.

questions.prompt: A balanced equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides.
A balanced equation always has the same number of molecules on each side.
questions.explanation: False — it means equal atoms of each element, not molecules.

questions.prompt: The state symbol (aq) means a substance is dissolved in water.
The state symbol (g) means a solid.
In a synthesis reaction, two substances combine to make one new substance.
No energy is required in a decomposition reaction.
questions.explanation: False — energy (often heat) is needed to break the bonds.

questions.prompt: Thermal decomposition uses heat to break down a compound.
A more reactive element can displace a less reactive one.
Hydrogen can displace zinc from a compound.
questions.explanation: False — zinc is more reactive, so zinc displaces hydrogen, not the other way round.

questions.prompt: In double displacement, two compounds swap partners to make two new compounds.
Barium sulphate is soluble and stays in solution.
questions.explanation: False — barium sulphate is insoluble and forms a precipitate.

questions.prompt: Combustion is another word for burning.
Burning a hydrocarbon produces carbon dioxide and water.
Endothermic reactions take in heat, so the surroundings get colder.
Exothermic reactions take in heat from the surroundings.
questions.explanation: False — exothermic reactions give out heat.

questions.prompt: Photosynthesis is an exothermic reaction.
questions.explanation: False — photosynthesis is endothermic (it takes in light energy).

questions.prompt: Rusting is an exothermic reaction.
questions.explanation: True — it gives out heat, slowly.

questions.prompt: Respiration is an endothermic reaction.
questions.explanation: False — respiration is exothermic (it releases energy).

questions.prompt: Neutralisation is an exothermic reaction.
questions.explanation: True — it gives out a small amount of heat.

questions.prompt: A cation is a positive ion.
An anion is formed when an atom loses an electron.
questions.explanation: False — an anion forms when an atom gains an electron.

questions.prompt: Ionic bonds are very strong.
Solid ionic compounds conduct electricity.
questions.explanation: False — they conduct only when molten or dissolved.

questions.prompt: Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.
questions.explanation: True — because the bonds are strong.

questions.prompt: Ionic compounds form when a metal reacts with a non-metal.
In a covalent bond, electrons are shared.
Most covalent compounds have high melting points.
questions.explanation: False — they have low melting points because forces between molecules are weak.

questions.prompt: Covalent compounds can conduct electricity.
questions.explanation: False — they have no free charged particles.

questions.prompt: Water is a polar molecule.
questions.explanation: True — slightly + at one end, slightly − at the other.

questions.prompt: Water is a good solvent because it is polar.
Hydrogen gas is given off when a reactive metal reacts with an acid.
Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.
Carbon dioxide is lighter than air.
questions.explanation: False — carbon dioxide is heavier than air.

questions.prompt: Magnesium forms the ion Mg²⁺ by losing two electrons.
Sodium chloride has the formula NaCl.
Magnesium oxide has the formula MgO₂.
Reactants are the new substances made in a reaction.
questions.explanation: False — reactants are the starting substances; products are the new substances.
